C1.rationale: The unit imposes almost no directives: it explicitly disclaims prescriptive force and frames every entry as a 'Use when' condition that selects a word rather than a prohibition on other words, which is the delegated-judgment shape the anchor rewards. It falls short of 5 only because the few constraints it does carry (the four-step 'Extending' list) are glossary bookkeeping rather than load-bearing rules that generalise.

evidence.quote: The list is descriptive of current practice, not prescriptive: extend it as the vocabulary matures.

C2.rationale: The unit is a narrative/definitional reference with no invocation interface — no arguments, flags, or parameters to make self-describing. The rubric directs 'a pure narrative reference is n/a'.

C3.rationale: One flat always-loaded file carries everything: seven full reference tables, a meta-section explaining how to read a three-column table, and a maintenance procedure that only matters on the rare occasion someone adds a term — none of it split into a separately-loadable surface. The only disclosure gesture is pushing plugin-specific terms outward to plugin rules, which keeps it above anchor 1 but well short of competent.

C4.rationale: Ownership is unusually explicit for a glossary: it names where plugin-specific vocabulary must live instead, cross-links rather than restating (parallel-agent-dispatch, agent-development, conventional-commits), and openly flags the one acknowledged overlap. Short of 5 because a handful of entries (Fan-out agents, Spin up a subagent, Checkpoint, Adversarial review) do re-define concepts already owned by named plugin skills the file itself points at.

evidence.quote: If the term is plugin-specific (e.g. blueprint's `ADR`, `PRD`, `PRP`), keep it in that plugin's rules and cross-link instead.

C5.rationale: This is the anchor-1 case almost exactly: ~55 definitions loaded into every turn of every session, the overwhelming majority of which state the obvious to a Claude 5 generation model. Nothing in 'Code operations' (hoist, lift, extract, inline, refactor in place, normalize), 'Requirements framing' (user story, happy path, edge cases, invariants, acceptance criteria), or 'Work state' (resume, park, unblock, stage) redefines a term against its universal software meaning — a capable model already uses every one of them correctly without being told. Perhaps five entries carry any house-specific hook, and the file also inlines a maintenance procedure that only matters when a term is being added. Almost none of it must hold on a turn where the user asked about something else.

| Happy path | The nominal flow when nothing goes wrong | Establishing the baseline behaviour first |

C6.rationale: Genuinely narrative material — definitions and disambiguating conditions are not mechanical work a script or schema could state more exactly, so the dimension applies only weakly and the unit is not penalised. It does point at the higher-fidelity artifacts that own the concepts (plugin skills and sibling rules) by name rather than re-describing their behaviour in prose.

top_finding: Move the glossary off the always-loaded surface — path-scope it or promote it to an on-demand skill referenced by name — and keep in context only the handful of entries whose meaning is house-specific rather than universal software vocabulary.
counter_finding: The explicit ownership boundary — plugin-specific vocabulary stays in that plugin's rules and cross-links back here — is real single-source-of-truth discipline that tells a future edit where to land, and should survive any trimming.
